domain: Nuclear Power Station SCADA & Industrial Control (ICS)
title: $18.5M Unit 2/3 SCADA Modernization and IEC 62443 Compliance Program
executive_summary: Meridian Controls proposes a fixed-price $18.5M turnkey modernization of Unit 2 and Unit 3 SCADA to deliver deterministic telemetry and IEC 62443 compliance within 90 days. Technical review reveals critical conflicts around air-gapping, safety validation, and patching that create licensing and nuclear safety risk.

proposal_document.title: Commercial Proposal v1.0
proposal_document.text:
Meridian Controls proposes a turnkey SCADA modernization for Unit 2 and Unit 3 delivering deterministic telemetry at 50ms scan cycles across 12,000 I/O points with 99.999% historian availability, fully air-gapped with unidirectional data diodes and certified IEC 62443 SL-T3 compliant out-of-the-box. The system guarantees zero-downtime cutover with live migration and 24/7 remote vendor support via secure VPN for predictive maintenance.

The solution provides real-time automated safety interlock validation every 100ms, unlimited historian retention for 10 years at full resolution, and guaranteed 15-minute emergency patch deployment for all controllers without requiring outage or NRC re-validation. All commissioning will be completed within 90 days with fixed-price $18.5M inclusive of licensing, hardware, and 5-year support.

technical_specification.title: Technical Architecture Spec v4.2
technical_specification.text:
The architecture implements redundant ControlLogix-based controllers on an isolated Level 3.5 DMZ with unidirectional data diodes, providing deterministic telemetry at 50ms scan cycles across 12,000 I/O points with 99.999% historian availability measured per historian cluster. Per IEC 62443-3-3 SR 5.4 and site security plan SSP-09, the safety OT network shall remain physically air-gapped with all remote access and VPN ports disabled by default, requiring on-site access via monitored KVM and escorted maintenance windows.

Safety interlock proof-testing requires manual validation during scheduled refueling outages with a 36-month proof-test interval and 12-hour maintenance window per train, with automated diagnostics limited to non-safety heartbeat monitoring at 500ms intervals. Emergency controller patches require an 8-hour outage window per unit plus NRC 10 CFR 50.59 evaluation and re-validation averaging 14 days, with phased commissioning over 180 days across Unit 2 and Unit 3 during planned outages only.

commitments.claim: Fully air-gapped system with 24/7 remote vendor VPN support
commitments.proposal_quote: 24/7 remote vendor support via secure VPN for predictive maintenance
commitments.spec_quote: shall remain physically air-gapped with all remote access and VPN ports disabled by default
commitments.explanation: Proposal promises persistent remote VPN access while spec mandates physical air-gap with VPN disabled by default and only on-site KVM access, which cannot be satisfied simultaneously under IEC 62443 and site security plan.

commitments.claim: Unlimited 10-year historian retention at full resolution
commitments.proposal_quote: unlimited historian retention for 10 years at full resolution
commitments.explanation: Spec defines only historian availability per cluster and scan performance, with no retention duration, resolution, storage sizing, or data compression policy to support a 10-year unlimited full-resolution commitment.

commitments.claim: Real-time automated safety interlock validation every 100ms
commitments.proposal_quote: real-time automated safety interlock validation every 100ms
commitments.spec_quote: automated diagnostics limited to non-safety heartbeat monitoring at 500ms intervals
commitments.explanation: Proposal is vague on whether automation applies to safety-rated interlocks versus non-safety diagnostics; spec limits automation to non-safety heartbeat at 500ms and requires manual proof-testing for safety interlocks, leaving scope and safety-credit uncertainty.

commitments.claim: Deterministic 50ms scan telemetry across 12,000 I/O points
commitments.proposal_quote: deterministic telemetry at 50ms scan cycles across 12,000 I/O points
commitments.spec_quote: providing deterministic telemetry at 50ms scan cycles across 12,000 I/O points with 99.999% historian availability measured per historian cluster
commitments.explanation: Spec explicitly confirms the same scan rate, I/O count, and availability metric claimed in the proposal for the redundant controller architecture.
